hero.heading: Overcoming divisions between the law and tenancy realities
hero.lead: Homes Without Divisions is a community legal empowerment initiative by Pro Bono HK for tenants living in subdivided units. Our mission is to advance the next generation of equitable tenancy in Hong Kong.

mission.heading: The universal right to adequate housing
body: Article 39 of the Basic Law provides that the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights is fully in force in Hong Kong. Article 11(1) of the ICESCR provides the universal right to adequate housing. According to the Guidelines for the Implementation on the Right to Adequate Housing by the Special Rapporteur, this includes security of tenure, availability of services, affordability, habitability, accessibility, appropriate location and cultural adequacy.

Our mission is to advance the next generation of equitable tenancy in Hong Kong, by adopting and facilitating both international legal standards and domestic regulations, especially in view of the recent Basic Housing Units reform in the city.
mission.methodsHeading: We do this in two ways

methods.name: Standard-setting
methods.body: First, we set a common standard, by publishing a model tenancy agreement and supporting documents that any tenant and landlord can adopt.

methods.name: Capacity-building
methods.body: Second, we build capacity, by explaining what the law already gives you and how to use it.

pillars.heading: The three pillars of an equitable tenancy
pillars.lead: We design this project around an equitable tenancy philosophy in mind: transparent communication, fair terms and conduct, and appropriate solution, with the corresponding resources for you.
pillars.diagramDescription: Three overlapping circles representing transparent communication, fair terms and conduct, and appropriate solution. Where all three overlap is a human-oriented equitable tenancy. Two dotted circles around the outside mark our two ways of working: standard-setting and capacity-building.

capability.heading: A humanist perspective on law
body: The Without Divisions ethos is grounded in a humanist perspective on law. It is inspired by the capability approach to human welfare and development theorised by Amartya Sen and other scholars. We notice how, despite formal legal protections, it is often difficult to translate them across the fabric of society into meaningful empowerment.

The capability approach emphasises the role of “freedom to achieve” by our human agency, which is directly relevant in the contexts of access to justice and the rule of law. It reminds us that what is right or good does not just come with a list of rights, or because it has always been how it works. It is more about how we, with help from the community, strive for opportunities and capacity for improvement to live a better life.

For tenants in subdivided units, this means not only having statutory protections on paper or top of their mind, but also being able to understand their tenancies, communicate with fair terms and conduct, seek solutions without worries, and exercise agency in daily decision-making of navigating tenancy relationships.

We hope that whoever you are reading this — whether a subdivided units tenant, a frontline NGO worker, a person who is going to live in a subdivided unit, or a member of the general public who is curious — these resources would meaningfully help you in pointing the right direction when you have to make the choice next time.

communication.name: Transparent communication
communication.body: You talk about and discuss the tenancy openly, clearly, and in good time. Transparency reduces uncertainty and prevents misunderstandings.

terms.name: Fair terms and conduct
terms.body: Your tenancy agreement is reasonable and does not contain illegal terms, and it reflects good faith and respect from both sides.

solution.name: Appropriate solution
solution.body: You know what to do, and you know how the law can help when issues come up or before things go wrong.

schedule-of-condition.name: Schedule of Condition
schedule-of-condition.when: Before you enter into a tenancy
schedule-of-condition.summary: Ask your landlord or estate agent to fill this in before signing, to check on the property conditions and provide important tenancy information.
points: Check and record the condition of each item. If something needs repair or is missing, ask the Landlord to fix it
Check and ask the Landlord for any common area access
Ask the Landlord important questions in the rest of the form, so you know what you are getting into

model-tenancy-agreement.name: Model Tenancy Agreement
model-tenancy-agreement.summary: Party-neutral drafting verified by lawyers that aims to accurately reflect the statutory reality. It does not impose extra burden on either landlord or tenant beyond what is required under the law.
points: Many common stationery-shop templates contain invalid or even illegal terms that do not apply to subdivided units letting
Drafted in plain language while retaining legal accuracy, avoiding unnecessary legalese
Optional Addenda covering transitional arrangements under the Basic Housing Units policy, landlord's agents, and more

pocket-tenancy-clinic.name: Pocket Tenancy Clinic
pocket-tenancy-clinic.nameSecondary: 分間單位租務解難手冊
pocket-tenancy-clinic.when: When issues come up, or before things go wrong
pocket-tenancy-clinic.summary: An interactive pocket clinic that simulates the intake, diagnostic and treatment processes of a working pro bono clinic, rather than a static list of rights to be read once.
points: A Tenancy Risk Diagnostics Form, to see where your tenancy stands
Ten colour-coded Treatment Rooms for the top ten tenancy issues
Two further Emergency Rooms, each with concrete action steps
